title: The stars rated your profile.
old_caption:
Eight judges, five fish photos, and zero clues about who's holding them. The panel wasn't unkind, just curious about you.
Lead your profile with who you are, not what you caught.

title: Red Flag, Green Flag.
old_caption: One star's red flag is another's green. That's okay. What matters is knowing your own and saying them early. Telling someone your dealbreakers up front is a kindness to you both.

title: Neptune is literally fog.
old_caption:
When you're glowing about someone new, it can be hard to see clearly. Friends who care will gently point out what you're missing.
If everyone you trust sees the same flag, it's worth listening.

title: Dear ghoster…
old_caption:
Thinking about just not answering them?
A kind goodbye takes ten seconds. Nobody deserves to be left on delivered.

title: The Protocol
old_caption: Not feeling a match? Disappearing leaves someone wondering for weeks. One kind sentence lets you both move on with care. It's short, it's honest, and it's enough.

title: ✨her date tonight✨
old_caption: Your friends researched everything about your date except what he looks like, and somehow they're already planning a wedding. Real chemistry starts with words. Let the conversation lead.

title: The Group Chat
old_caption:
One "had fun!" text, twelve friends, ninety-nine opinions. It's easy to lose your own voice in all that love.
Your friends care about you, but your gut knows you. Say what you actually want to say.

title: Love Gym.
old_caption: "I missed you." "That hurt." "I like you." Saying feelings out loud can feel heavy at first. Like any muscle, it gets easier with practice. "It's fine" doesn't count as a rep.

title: Captain Boundaries.
old_caption:
If saying yes to everyone has left you running on empty, meet Captain Boundaries. Their power is a kind, clear no.
Your feelings are valid. A boundary set early saves a lot of hurt later.

title: hey
old_caption:
Every sign reacts to a lonely "hey" in their own way, from instant plans to six unsent drafts.
If you want a real reply, send a real question. Effort is attractive, and it shows you care.
